aws_cis_ec2_default_security_group_not_a.summary: Replace the attached default security group with approved application groups.
steps: Inspect the reported instance and every attached network interface; identify the exact same-VPC group ID whose GroupName is default.
Review required application traffic and prepare approved replacement groups with only the needed ingress and egress rules.
Apply the reviewed group association change to each affected interface, validate application connectivity, then recollect the instance and security-group inventory.
caveats: Removing a group before approved replacement rules are ready can interrupt traffic; coordinate the change with the workload owner.
The group name is only a configuration label; this check does not prove that the default group permits public ingress.

aws_g6_ec2_instance_no_public_ipv6.summary: Review and remove unneeded globally routable IPv6 assignments from the instance.
steps: Identify the reported attached network interface and exact globally routable IPv6 address, and check whether the workload requires that address.
Review traffic, DNS records, route tables, and security-group rules with the workload owner before changing the assignment.
Remove an unneeded IPv6 assignment through the approved interface change, verify required connectivity, and recollect the instance.
caveats: An assigned global IPv6 address does not prove public reachability; effective exposure also depends on routes, security groups, and a listening service.
Removing an address can disrupt traffic or DNS clients; preserve required connectivity during the change.
